claim: Polya heuristics as named labels are descriptive, not prescriptive: one label (for example specialise) hides several different procedures, so a bare menu entry does not tell the model how to act.
schema_part: O1-O8 (each operator needs a concrete procedure plus a trigger)
agent_test: Operator given as label only vs label plus procedure plus trigger, equal tokens, fixed problem set.

claim: Early classroom studies (1960s-70s) found taught heuristics did not transfer and gave small gains; strategies are problem- and student-specific (Begle). Later meta-analysis (Hembree, 487 reports) found gains mainly in middle and later grades. Hembree abstract (re-read in gap search): no method superior in K-5, heuristics mildly better in 6-8, distinctly superior in high school, diagram/representation training gave the largest gain. Effect sizes still not obtained.
schema_part: G (do not force one strategy on every problem)
agent_test: One fixed heuristic prompt vs problem-adaptive selection, equal tokens.
audit_note: Schoenfeld reports 'little empirical evidence' and only relatively small correlations rather than 'small gains' from taught heuristics; Hembree abstract verified via Crossref (487 reports, grade pattern, diagrams largest gain).

claim: Heuristics need control. In more than 100 videotaped attempts about 60% of novice attempts were 'read, pick a direction, never check', versus under 20% after a semester of control prompts (what are you doing, why, how does it help). One chapter, no N or test statistic reported.
schema_part: G (progress and monitoring guardrails); S-states for checking
agent_test: Insert a periodic what/why/how-does-it-help self-check every K steps vs none, equal tokens; count persistence on dead ends.

claim: Explicit heuristic training beat practice-only and no-training in a replication of Schoenfeld 1979 (Rott and Gawlick 2014, re-opened: n=9/10/9, ANCOVA F=6.593 p=0.005; corrected d explicit vs practice 0.79, vs test-only 1.44; practice vs test-only 0.64; explicit pre-post d 0.88). Original had n=7 and no test-only group. The replication itself is small (about 10 per cell, maths teacher students, posttest harder than pretest). No larger replication found.
schema_part: memory/O (worked examples with heuristic annotations)
agent_test: In-context worked solutions annotated with heuristic names vs unannotated, equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Direct teaching matters: practice without explicit heuristic instruction did not help, and rigid step-by-step procedures did worse than flexible approaches (Hembree via Bruun; effect sizes not read). Chess transfer to maths appeared only when heuristics were taught (d=0.50 vs 0.20 vs control 0.13, N=931).
schema_part: G (flexible use, not rigid scripts)
agent_test: Rigid fixed-order plan vs flexible menu, equal tokens.

claim: Drilling a heuristic turns it into an algorithm and removes its heuristic character.
schema_part: none (design note: avoid over-scripting operators)
agent_test: Rigid vs optional operator use; compare outcomes.

claim: Competing explanation: expert success may rest on stored problem schemas rather than general heuristics; template retrieval (Buffer of Thoughts) is the machine version.
schema_part: memory (retrieval of past problem templates)
agent_test: Template retrieval vs generic heuristic menu on held-out problems.

claim: A plan-then-solve trigger beats zero-shot CoT on arithmetic with text-davinci-003: six-set average 70.4 (CoT), 72.9 (PS), 76.7 (PS+); GSM8K 56.4/58.2/59.3. Re-verified in the paper table. PS+ roughly equals 8-shot manual CoT (77.6) and does not beat it. GPT-3-era model, wording-sensitive.
schema_part: S (plan state) / O1
agent_test: Plan-first prompt vs plain CoT, equal tokens, held-out maths with the target model.

claim: Planning reduces calculation and missing-step errors slightly but not semantic misunderstanding (GSM8K, 100 items: semantic errors 27% CoT, 26% PS, 27% PS+; wrong answers 46/43/39).
schema_part: G (understand-first check), S0
agent_test: Add a restate-and-check-understanding step; measure semantic-error share.

claim: Step-back (Polya generalise) gives large gains on physics and chemistry for weaker models (PaLM-2L 66.4 to 73.2, 70.9 to 81.8) but little over CoT for GPT-4 (84.5 vs 82.9; 85.6 vs 85.3, inside the spread) and none on GSM8K (84.3 vs CoT 84.4). Re-verified for MMLU.
schema_part: O (abstraction operator, conditional on model strength and task)
agent_test: Step-back on/off by model strength and task type, equal tokens.

claim: Abstraction itself rarely fails; reasoning after it does. Step-back fixes 20.5% of baseline errors and adds 11.9% new ones on MMLU physics; over 90% of residual errors are in the reasoning step. Re-verified (20.5/11.9).
schema_part: G (verify after abstraction), O verify
agent_test: Verification step after step-back; count introduced errors.

claim: Decomposition into sub-problems (least-to-most) is huge on compositional length generalisation (SCAN length 16.2 CoT to 99.7) but small on GSM8K (60.87 to 62.39): worse at 2 steps (76.68 vs 74.53), better at 5+ steps (39.07 to 45.23). Re-verified. Hand-written decompositions fix nearly all failures, so choosing the decomposition is the bottleneck.
schema_part: O (decompose operator; trigger on step count or length)
agent_test: Decompose gated by estimated step count vs always-on, equal tokens.

claim: A model-chosen heuristic menu (Self-Discover, 39 modules) beats CoT: PaLM 2-L BBH 60 to 67, T4D 40 to 69, MATH 42 to 50.5; GPT-4 75 to 81, 52 to 85, 71 to 73. Beats direct on 23/25 and CoT on 21/25 tasks. Re-verified. Of 99 wrong MATH answers, 74.7% are computation errors and only 25.3% wrong structure.
schema_part: O menu: select, adapt, compose; plus separate compute check
agent_test: Once-per-task menu selection vs none, equal tokens; add code or calculator check for compute errors.

claim: Self-generated related problems (analogical prompting) gain 1 to 3 points over CoT on strong chat models (GSM8K GPT-3.5: 75.8 0-shot CoT, 76.7 5-shot, 77.8 ours; MATH 33.9/34.9/37.3) and up to 10.7 on text-davinci-003 (50.3/54.0/61.0). Gain shrinks with model strength.
schema_part: O (related-problem operator)
agent_test: Self-generated analogues vs none, equal tokens; check the gain shrinks with model strength.

claim: Working backwards is much harder for models than solving forward: GSM8K GPT-4 92.8 vs 38.6, PaLM-2 58.4 vs 10.8, LLaMa-2-70B 60.5 vs 15.2 (re-verified). Rewriting into a forward problem gave 10 to 20 point gains.
schema_part: O (work-backwards operator should first convert to forward form)
agent_test: Backward-form tasks: direct vs reformulate-to-forward, equal tokens.

claim: Hints help only when correct: human-style hints beat CoT on MATH; wrong or random hints fall below CoT.
schema_part: G (do not trust a self-generated hint without a check)
agent_test: Inject correct, vague and wrong hints; measure the drop.

claim: Benefit of a given Polya heuristic depends on problem type and model; some heuristics hurt small models (informal blog, no n). Strong models gain little from added menus. New: no single strategy wins across problem slices (PRISM, trained 7-8B models: one strategy ranges 13.5 to 95.3 across datasets); instance-level vs task-level planning flips with task uniformity (iSelf-Discover). Still no hand-written selection rule tested.
schema_part: G (selection and precondition rule per operator)
agent_test: Per-problem-type heuristic selection vs all-on, equal tokens.

claim: Putting 11 heuristic families in the RL rollout prompt (name a heuristic before each step) improved 14 of 15 model-by-test comparisons on MATH-Perturb and others; hard perturbations cut accuracy by 10 to 30 points. Anonymous preprint.
schema_part: O (name heuristic before step)
agent_test: Name-heuristic-before-step prompt on perturbed problems.

claim: Polya-like behaviours (backtracking, verification, subgoals, backward chaining) in the starting model predict RL gain; backtracking mattered most and correctness of priming content mattered little.
schema_part: O verify/backtrack
agent_test: Explicit backtrack prompt vs none, equal tokens.

claim: Fine-tuning on Polya-staged tutoring dialogues balances stage use but no accuracy gain was measured; stacking with MetaMath interfered.
schema_part: none (training, out of scope)
agent_test: Not testable without training.

claim: Combining methods with different solved sets beats either alone (AlphaGeometry 25/30, Wu+DD+AR 21/30, Wu+AG 27/30); random auxiliary points plus heuristics reach 28/30 (HAGeo).
schema_part: O (auxiliary construction; union of diverse attempts)
agent_test: Two complementary strategies plus a verifier vs one strategy, equal tokens.

claim: Frontier models find fewer distinct strategies than people despite near-ceiling accuracy (80 AMC/AIME problems, 217 reference strategies; Claude Opus 4.6 found 110, Gemini 184).
schema_part: O (strategy diversification)
agent_test: Prompt for distinct strategies; count distinct approaches vs accuracy.

claim: Routing a strategy per problem helps modestly (PRISM +3.1 on MATH) and is capped by classifier accuracy (predicted categories 29% below true-category routing). Gap search detail: PRISM gain over best single strategy is +0.9 (Qwen2.5-Math-7B), +2.9, +7.6 (Llama-3-8B), shrinking as the base model gets stronger; the router lost on AQuA; the ensemble baseline looks mis-tuned.
schema_part: G/O selection rule
agent_test: Measure selection accuracy as the ceiling for menu routing.

claim: Polya-style retrieved heuristics raised process quality of LLM solutions less than persona prompting (RAG positive but not significant); CoT and RAG about doubled odds of high process quality vs zero-shot (2880 solutions).
schema_part: O menu vs persona
agent_test: Heuristic retrieval vs persona prompt on process quality.

claim: On non-reasoning models of 2023-24, a model checking its own reasoning without outside information does not help and can hurt: GSM8K GPT-4 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0 over two self-correction rounds, GPT-3.5 75.9 to 74.7; pointing to the first wrong step is hard (best overall 52.87%, GPT-4) and gets worse with more calls per trace (more false alarms). Telling the model the true error location lets it fix a substantial minority of wrong traces (+18 to +44 percent of wrong traces corrected, depending on task), but a random location breaks 7 to 16 percent of right traces.
schema_part: G (progress and monitoring guardrails): checks must be concrete and gated; a vague 'are you sure' check is harmful on weaker models
agent_test: Control step as concrete test (recompute, special case, bound) vs generic 'review' prompt vs no control, on a current reasoning model, equal tokens, report false-alarm rate (right answers changed to wrong).
audit_note: Numbers verified, but Tyen et al. report that with the true error location 18 to 44 percent of originally wrong traces become correct, which is not 'most' wrong traces.
claim_before_audit: On non-reasoning models of 2023-24, a model checking its own reasoning without outside information does not help and can hurt: GSM8K GPT-4 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0 over two self-correction rounds, GPT-3.5 75.9 to 74.7; pointing to the first wrong step is hard (best overall 52.87%, GPT-4) and gets worse with more calls per trace (more false alarms). Telling the model the true error location lets it fix most wrong traces (+18 to +44 points), but a random location breaks 7 to 16 points of right traces.

claim: Current reasoning models notice errors much better than 2023 chat models: ProcessBench first-error F1 average GPT-4o 61.9, QwQ-32B-Preview 71.5, o1-mini 87.9, and all fall on olympiad problems (GPT-4o 79.2 on GSM8K to 51.4 on OlympiadBench). This is judging another solution, not a live self-check.
schema_part: O (verify/control operators): a control step may now be worth its tokens on reasoning models
agent_test: Same model checks (a) its own live attempt every k steps, (b) a finished attempt, (c) a different model's attempt; compare dead-end detection.

claim: Generic chain-of-thought prompting on dedicated reasoning models gives marginal or mixed gains: GPQA Diamond (198 questions x 25 trials) o3-mini +2.9 points, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3, for 20-80% more time; other procedure prompts (decompose, weigh three paths) made negligible difference on GPT-4o. A study on distilled R1 models (1.5B-32B) found CoT prompts helped in 72% of cases and cut reflection loops, but its 'direct' baseline suppresses thinking. A 39-problem Grok-4.1 test is inside noise.
schema_part: Whole schema: any prompt scaffold must beat 'no scaffold' at equal tokens on a reasoning model; log thinking tokens as well as accuracy
agent_test: O1-O5 menu vs bare problem on a reasoning model, 25+ samples per problem, paired test, equal-token budget.

claim: Spreading attempts over several distinct named approaches beats spending the same calls on one prompt, on non-reasoning models: TTS-Uniform (strategy list then equal sampling) lifts GPT-4.1-mini AIME 2024 Acc@32 from 60.0 (self-consistency) to 73.3 and GPT-4o-mini AIME 2025 from 3.3 to 23.3 at the same sample count; DIV-SE (5 approach prompts) lifts GPT-4 Graph Coloring from 15 (CoT) and 23 (SC-10) to 97, with gains vanishing on GPT-3.5 planning and LLaMA-2 zero-shot where the model cannot follow the approach. Both use majority vote, not a verifier. In TTS the gain is smaller for the stronger GPT-4.1-mini than for GPT-4o-mini, but DIV-SE needs a model strong enough to follow the approach prompts.
schema_part: O (operator menu used for diversity) and the stopping/aggregation rule
agent_test: k attempts each with a different O1-O5 operator vs k plain samples, majority vote vs verifier selection, equal tokens, on a reasoning model.
audit_note: All numbers verified (TTS 60.0 to 73.3, 3.3 to 23.3; DIV-SE 15/23 to 97, GPT-3.5 Blocksworld no gain, LLaMA-2 ZS-CoT 31.32 to 32.00), but 'gains shrink as the base model gets stronger' holds only within TTS and is contradicted at the weak end by DIV-SE, where weaker models gain nothing.
claim_before_audit: Spreading attempts over several distinct named approaches beats spending the same calls on one prompt, on non-reasoning models: TTS-Uniform (strategy list then equal sampling) lifts GPT-4.1-mini AIME 2024 Acc@32 from 60.0 (self-consistency) to 73.3 and GPT-4o-mini AIME 2025 from 3.3 to 23.3 at the same sample count; DIV-SE (5 approach prompts) lifts GPT-4 Graph Coloring from 15 (CoT) and 23 (SC-10) to 97, with gains vanishing on GPT-3.5 planning and LLaMA-2 zero-shot where the model cannot follow the approach. Both use majority vote, not a verifier. Gains shrink as the base model gets stronger.

claim: Backward reasoning helps mainly as a check or as a reformulation, not as a way to solve. FOBAR (mask a number, give the candidate answer, ask for the number) adds about 1 to 2 points average over self-consistency (davinci 81.4 to 83.5; ComplexCoT 83.2 to 85.0; GPT-3.5-Turbo 85.5 to 86.6) using extra backward chains. RevThink trains on model-written backward questions: Mistral-7B GSM8K 59.08 (best augmentation baseline) to 60.88, test-time still forward only. Neither tests a prompt at equal tokens.
schema_part: O (work backwards) reformulated as: write the forward question whose answer is the target; and as a substitution check in the verify step
agent_test: Work-backwards as direct prompt vs as reformulate-to-forward vs as substitution check, equal tokens, on problems with a numeric target.

claim: Write plans in prose, not in rigid structure: the same Self-Discover plan as free text beat JSON on MATH (200 problems) by 12 points on LLaMA-3.1-405B (75.5 vs 63.5) and 9 points on Mistral-Large (76.5 vs 67.5). Fresh per-problem plans beat one task-level plan on the mixed BBH set but lost badly on the uniform T4D set (100.0 vs 73-79).
schema_part: Plan state and operator menu wording (section on how the schema is rendered to the model)
agent_test: Plan as prose vs plan as JSON fields, same content, equal tokens, reasoning model; per-problem plan vs reusable plan on uniform vs mixed problem sets.
